boards.title: 10 Late-Night Runs That Explain Salisbury University
boards.description: Ten currently documented, under-21-safe food destinations in Salisbury with late operating hours.

cards.title: Taco Bell on North Salisbury Boulevard
cards.subtitle: 2400 N Salisbury Blvd, Salisbury, MD
cards.notes: Use the drive-thru when you need a late food pickup; confirm the day’s hours before leaving because closing times vary by day.
cards.short_summary: A North Salisbury Boulevard option with drive-thru service documented into the early morning.
cards.evidence_claim: Taco Bell lists drive-thru hours until 1 a.m. Sunday–Thursday and 2 a.m. Friday–Saturday at 2400 N Salisbury Blvd.
cards.source_title: Taco Bell — 2400 N Salisbury Blvd, Salisbury
cards.access_notes: Drive-thru: 9 a.m.–1 a.m. Sunday–Thursday; 9 a.m.–2 a.m. Friday–Saturday, per the location page.

cards.title: Wendy’s on South Salisbury Boulevard
cards.subtitle: 1101 S Salisbury Blvd, Salisbury, MD
cards.notes: Choose this South Salisbury Boulevard location for a late drive-thru or restaurant stop, and check holiday-hour notices before a special-date visit.
cards.short_summary: A daily late-hours location on the south side of Salisbury.
cards.evidence_claim: Wendy’s lists both restaurant and drive-thru hours of 4 a.m.–3:59 a.m. daily at 1101 S Salisbury Blvd.
cards.access_notes: Restaurant and drive-thru hours are listed as 4 a.m.–3:59 a.m. daily; holiday hours may vary.

cards.title: Wendy’s at North Point
cards.subtitle: 2710 N Salisbury Blvd, Salisbury, MD
cards.notes: For a north-side late stop, use the restaurant or drive-thru and verify the posted schedule before traveling during holidays or disruptions.
cards.short_summary: A North Salisbury Boulevard location whose restaurant and drive-thru are listed until 3 a.m.
cards.evidence_claim: Wendy’s lists restaurant and drive-thru hours of 6:30 a.m.–3 a.m. daily at 2710 N Salisbury Blvd.
cards.access_notes: Restaurant and drive-thru hours are listed as 6:30 a.m.–3 a.m. daily.

cards.title: IHOP at North Point Plaza
cards.subtitle: 2732 N Salisbury Blvd, Salisbury, MD
cards.notes: Plan a Friday or Saturday evening visit for the latest listed service, or use its takeout and delivery options when a sit-down meal is not practical.
cards.short_summary: An all-day-breakfast restaurant with midnight Friday and Saturday hours.
cards.evidence_claim: IHOP lists hours until midnight Friday and Saturday at 2732 N Salisbury Blvd; other days close at 10 p.m.
cards.access_notes: Listed hours: 6 a.m.–midnight Friday and Saturday; 6 a.m.–10 p.m. Sunday–Thursday.

cards.title: Denny’s on Punkin Court
cards.subtitle: 405 Punkin Court, Salisbury, MD
cards.notes: Use the official location page to confirm the daily schedule, then choose dine-in or takeout for a late dinner or breakfast-style meal.
cards.short_summary: A diner listed open until 11 p.m. every day in Salisbury.
cards.evidence_claim: Denny’s lists restaurant hours of 6 a.m.–11 p.m. daily at 405 Punkin Court.
cards.access_notes: Restaurant hours are listed as 6 a.m.–11 p.m. daily; the location advises confirming hours directly.

cards.title: Domino’s on South Salisbury Boulevard
cards.subtitle: 1121 S Salisbury Blvd, Salisbury, MD
cards.notes: Order pickup or delivery from this South Salisbury Boulevard store, checking the live location page for the day’s closing time before placing an order.
cards.short_summary: A south-side pizza pickup or delivery option documented until midnight.
cards.evidence_claim: Domino’s lists its 1121 S Salisbury Blvd location as open until 12 a.m. on the location page.
cards.access_notes: The live location page lists the store open until 12 a.m.; Domino’s notes that hours vary by location.

cards.title: Domino’s on North Salisbury Road
cards.subtitle: 1730 N Salisbury Road, Salisbury, MD
cards.notes: Select this distinct North Salisbury Road store for pickup or delivery and check its live listing when timing a late order.
cards.short_summary: A separate Salisbury Domino’s location listed open until 1 a.m.
cards.evidence_claim: Domino’s Salisbury location directory lists the 1730 N Salisbury Road store as open until 1 a.m.
cards.access_notes: The official Salisbury location directory lists this store open until 1 a.m.; verify the live order page before going.

cards.title: Pizza Hut on East Main Street
cards.subtitle: 830 E Main St, Salisbury, MD
cards.notes: Use the East Main Street location for a late pizza pickup or delivery order, and confirm that its live hours still match your planned arrival.
cards.short_summary: A Pizza Hut location listed open until 1 a.m. on Salisbury’s official store directory.
cards.evidence_claim: Pizza Hut’s Salisbury directory lists the 830 E Main St location as open until 1 a.m.
cards.access_notes: The official directory lists this location open until 1 a.m.; availability and hours should be checked when ordering.

cards.title: Pizza Hut at South Salisbury Boulevard
cards.subtitle: 1306 S Salisbury Blvd, Suite 172, Salisbury, MD
cards.notes: For an alternative late pizza order, select this South Salisbury Boulevard location and use the store directory to check the current closing time.
cards.short_summary: A second Salisbury Pizza Hut listed open until midnight.
cards.evidence_claim: Pizza Hut’s Salisbury directory lists the 1306 S Salisbury Blvd location as open until midnight.
cards.access_notes: The official directory lists this location open until midnight; verify current hours before travel or ordering.

cards.title: Chick-fil-A South Salisbury
cards.subtitle: 828 S Salisbury Blvd, Salisbury, MD
cards.notes: Use dine-in, carry-out, drive-thru, or delivery during its listed late evening window; it is closed Sundays, so plan another option then.
cards.short_summary: A South Salisbury Boulevard food stop with four service modes listed through 10 p.m. Monday–Saturday.
cards.evidence_claim: Chick-fil-A lists dine-in, carry-out, drive-thru, and delivery hours of 6:30 a.m.–10 p.m. Monday–Saturday at South Salisbury.
cards.access_notes: Dine-in, carry-out, drive-thru, and delivery are listed 6:30 a.m.–10 p.m. Monday–Saturday; closed Sunday.

boards.title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
boards.description: Ten named campus spaces for studying, collaborating, creating and connecting, grounded in Salisbury University’s current public information.

cards.title: Guerrieri Academic Commons
cards.subtitle: Main library and academic hub
cards.notes: Start at the main library when you need to switch between solo work, research help, technology and meeting up without crossing campus.
cards.short_summary: A four-floor campus hub that combines library resources, academic support and varied work settings.
cards.evidence_claim: Salisbury University identifies the Guerrieri Academic Commons as its main library and says students use it to study, research, collaborate, work on projects and meet friends.
cards.access_notes: A Gull Card is required during certain hours; visitors may enter during the library’s visitor access hours.

cards.entity_name: Guerrieri Academic Commons Group Study Rooms
cards.title: GAC Group Study Rooms
cards.subtitle: Second floor, Guerrieri Academic Commons
cards.notes: Reserve a room before a project meeting, then choose the size that fits your group and use the whiteboard and display together.
cards.short_summary: Thirteen reservable rooms support small-to-large group work in the Academic Commons.
cards.evidence_claim: SU Libraries lists 13 group study rooms on the GAC second floor, in sizes seating four, eight or 10, reservable by SU students, faculty and staff.
cards.source_title: Reserve a Study Room or Carrel | Salisbury University
cards.access_notes: Reservations are limited to Salisbury University students, faculty and staff.

cards.title: GAC Study Carrels
cards.subtitle: Third floor, Guerrieri Academic Commons
cards.notes: Choose a carrel when you need a quieter individual setup; reserve ahead for a specific desk or check first-come availability.
cards.short_summary: Enclosed individual desks in quiet GAC areas provide a focused study option.
cards.evidence_claim: SU Libraries says the GAC has 28 reservable third-floor study carrels plus first-come carrels, all in quiet areas with minimum noise.
cards.source_title: Reserve a Study Room or Carrel | Salisbury University
cards.access_notes: Reservable carrels may be booked for up to 14 days; additional carrels are first come, first served.

cards.entity_name: Guerrieri Academic Commons Third-Floor Reading Rooms
cards.title: Third-Floor Reading Rooms
cards.subtitle: Quiet reading areas in Guerrieri Academic Commons
cards.notes: Bring your laptop and settle into the third-floor reading areas when you want low conversation and fewer distractions than open seating.
cards.short_summary: Designated quiet reading areas sit alongside the library’s general collection.
cards.evidence_claim: SU Libraries designates the GAC’s third-floor reading areas as quiet spaces where talking above a whisper is not allowed.
cards.source_title: Technology in the Library | Salisbury University
cards.access_notes: Very few computers are available in these reading areas; bring a device or check out a laptop from the Library Service Desk.

cards.title: SU Libraries MakerLab
cards.subtitle: Room 118, Guerrieri Academic Commons
cards.notes: Use the MakerLab for a course prototype or personal design project, and plan around its available equipment before you arrive.
cards.short_summary: A campus creation space with 3D printers, scanners and a laser engraver.
cards.evidence_claim: SU Libraries describes the MakerLab in GAC Room 118 as a space for students, faculty and staff to create and design objects using 3D printers, scanners and a laser engraver.
cards.source_title: Technology in the Library | Salisbury University
cards.access_notes: The space serves Salisbury University students, faculty and staff; check the MakerLab information for equipment details.

cards.title: University Writing Center
cards.subtitle: Second floor, Guerrieri Academic Commons
cards.notes: Book time with a trained peer consultant when a paper or project is still taking shape, rather than waiting for a final draft.
cards.short_summary: Peer writing support for papers and projects at any stage of the writing process.
cards.evidence_claim: Salisbury University says the University Writing Center, on the GAC second floor, offers meetings with trained peer consultants for papers and projects at any stage.
cards.access_notes: Located on the second floor of the Guerrieri Academic Commons.

cards.title: Center for Student Achievement
cards.subtitle: Second floor, Guerrieri Academic Commons
cards.notes: Use this stop to connect coursework questions with tutoring, supplemental instruction, coaching or advising in one academic-support location.
cards.short_summary: An academic-support center inside the GAC serving undergraduate students.
cards.evidence_claim: SU reports that the Center for Student Achievement supports undergraduate students through supplemental instruction, tutoring, academic coaching and advising.
cards.source_title: Salisbury University Officially Breaks Ground on Patricia R. Guerrieri Academic Commons
cards.access_notes: Enter through the Center for Student Achievement’s main doors near the GAC second-floor main elevators.

cards.entity_name: Edward H. Nabb Research Center for Delmarva History and Culture
cards.title: Nabb Research Center
cards.subtitle: Fourth floor, Guerrieri Academic Commons
cards.notes: Visit when a class or personal project needs Delmarva-focused primary-source research; begin by identifying the historical question you want to pursue.
cards.short_summary: A fourth-floor humanities research center focused on Delmarva history and culture.
cards.evidence_claim: Salisbury University describes the Nabb Research Center as a humanities research laboratory for university students and locates it on the GAC fourth floor.
cards.access_notes: Located on the fourth floor of the Guerrieri Academic Commons.

cards.title: The Square
cards.subtitle: Red-brick area in front of Guerrieri Academic Commons
cards.notes: Use this central outdoor meeting point to orient a group before heading into the Commons, Student Union or nearby campus events.
cards.short_summary: A named red-brick gathering area directly in front of the Academic Commons.
cards.evidence_claim: Salisbury University’s orientation guide defines The Square as the red-brick area in front of the Guerrieri Academic Commons.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor campus space; use normal campus access practices and observe posted event or weather notices.

cards.title: Guerrieri Student Union
cards.subtitle: Campus meeting rooms, lounges and eateries
cards.notes: Choose the Union when your plan needs a lounge, meeting room or flexible event setting, then confirm room availability before gathering.
cards.short_summary: A campus hub with lounges, meeting space, a studio, flex space and eateries.
cards.evidence_claim: Salisbury University says the Guerrieri Student Union includes meeting spaces and lounges, a yoga/dance studio, a 400-seat flex area, 12 reservable rooms and two eateries.
cards.source_title: Conference Services Facilities Reservations | Salisbury University
cards.access_notes: Listed normal hours are Monday–Saturday 8 a.m.–midnight and Sunday noon–midnight; confirm changes with Conference Services.

boards.title: Zero Dollars: 10 Hangs That Cost Nothing
boards.description: No-admission activities and public-facing places in and around Salisbury University, with current source support for free access.

cards.title: See the Art Space
cards.subtitle: Guerrieri Student Union, second-floor concourse
cards.notes: Meet on the second-floor concourse to view the current artwork, then use the exhibit as an easy conversation starter.
cards.short_summary: A public, no-admission campus art stop.
cards.evidence_claim: Salisbury University states that admission to the Art Space is free and the public is invited.
cards.access_notes: Located in the Guerrieri Student Union’s second-floor concourse; campus visitors planning to park must register in advance for a free parking pass.

cards.title: Walk the Salisbury Zoo
cards.subtitle: 755 South Park Drive, Salisbury
cards.notes: Take the paved exhibit paths together and pause at the animal habitats for a low-key outdoor afternoon near campus.
cards.short_summary: A free-admission zoo beside Salisbury City Park.
cards.evidence_claim: The Salisbury Zoo states that it offers free admission and free parking.
cards.access_notes: The zoo lists daily hours of 9 a.m.–4:30 p.m., except Thanksgiving and Christmas; follow posted visitor guidance.

cards.entity_name: Harriet Tubman Statue and Historic Marker
cards.title: Visit the Harriet Tubman Statue
cards.subtitle: 1101 Camden Avenue, Salisbury University campus
cards.notes: Walk over to read the historic marker and spend a few minutes discussing the public-art installation and its local connection.
cards.short_summary: A free-admission historic marker and campus sculpture.
cards.evidence_claim: Maryland’s official tourism listing identifies the Harriet Tubman Statue and Historic Marker at Salisbury University as free admission.
cards.source_title: Harriet Tubman Statue and Historic Marker | Visit Maryland
cards.access_notes: Outdoor campus destination at 1101 Camden Avenue; visit during normal campus access and observe posted site guidance.

cards.title: Tour Poplar Hill Mansion
cards.subtitle: 117 Elizabeth Street, Salisbury
cards.notes: Plan a self-guided visit when the mansion is open, then compare the exhibits on local history and early-1800s life.
cards.short_summary: A free-admission historic-house museum downtown.
cards.evidence_claim: Maryland’s official tourism listing identifies Poplar Hill Mansion as a self-guided-tour site with free admission and free parking.
cards.access_notes: The listing directs visitors to check the mansion’s website for hours; confirm it is open before traveling.

cards.title: Cheer at a Baseball Home Game
cards.subtitle: Salisbury University athletics
cards.notes: Choose a regular-season home date on the athletics calendar, bring friends, and settle in to watch a full Sea Gull baseball game.
cards.short_summary: A no-cost way to follow Sea Gull baseball.
cards.evidence_claim: Salisbury University states that, except for football, men’s basketball and men’s lacrosse, athletics events are free unless ticketed for NCAA events.
cards.access_notes: Use the athletics calendar to confirm the home date; NCAA events may be ticketed and are excluded from this free option.

cards.title: Watch Sea Gull Softball
cards.subtitle: Salisbury University athletics
cards.notes: Pick a regular-season home game from the calendar and make it a relaxed group outing between classes or on a weekend.
cards.short_summary: Regular non-NCAA softball games are a free sports hang.
cards.evidence_claim: Salisbury University states that, except for football, men’s basketball and men’s lacrosse, athletics events are free unless ticketed for NCAA events.
cards.access_notes: Confirm the matchup is a regular home game on the athletics calendar; NCAA events may require tickets.

cards.title: Catch Field Hockey at Home
cards.subtitle: Salisbury University athletics
cards.notes: Check the schedule for a regular home contest and meet up before the opening whistle for an easy daytime campus activity.
cards.short_summary: A free regular-season Sea Gull field hockey outing.
cards.evidence_claim: Salisbury University states that, except for football, men’s basketball and men’s lacrosse, athletics events are free unless ticketed for NCAA events.
cards.access_notes: Confirm the game and venue through the athletics calendar; NCAA events may be ticketed.

cards.title: Watch Women’s Soccer
cards.subtitle: Salisbury University athletics
cards.notes: Use the athletics calendar to select a regular home match, then arrive together before kickoff to watch from the stands.
cards.short_summary: A free regular-season match for a group outing.
cards.evidence_claim: Salisbury University states that, except for football, men’s basketball and men’s lacrosse, athletics events are free unless ticketed for NCAA events.
cards.access_notes: Verify the match is a regular home contest on the athletics calendar; NCAA events may require tickets.

cards.title: See Women’s Basketball
cards.subtitle: Salisbury University athletics
cards.notes: Coordinate around a regular home tipoff and make a simple indoor hang of cheering for the Sea Gulls together.
cards.short_summary: A free regular-season women’s basketball game.
cards.evidence_claim: Salisbury University states that, except for football, men’s basketball and men’s lacrosse, athletics events are free unless ticketed for NCAA events.
cards.access_notes: Check the athletics calendar for date and venue; NCAA tournament games may be ticketed.

cards.title: Go to a Volleyball Match
cards.subtitle: Salisbury University athletics
cards.notes: Find a regular home match on the calendar, invite a few classmates, and stay for a set or the entire match.
cards.short_summary: A free regular-season Sea Gull volleyball hang.
cards.evidence_claim: Salisbury University states that, except for football, men’s basketball and men’s lacrosse, athletics events are free unless ticketed for NCAA events.
cards.access_notes: Confirm a regular home match through the athletics calendar; NCAA events may require tickets.

boards.title: Claimed by 9am: 10 Study Spots Worth Showing Up Early For
boards.description: Ten distinct, documented study environments across Salisbury University Libraries, with access details and specific work-friendly features.

cards.title: Third Floor South Reading Room
cards.subtitle: Guerrieri Academic Commons · third floor
cards.notes: Take the main elevator to floor three, enter the South Reading Room, and use its book-stack setting for a quiet individual work session.
cards.short_summary: A named third-floor reading room beside the A–HF general collection.
cards.evidence_claim: SU’s wayfinding page identifies the Third Floor South Reading Room as the location for book stacks with call numbers A–HF; the library designates third-floor stacks areas as quiet spaces.
cards.access_notes: Located in the Guerrieri Academic Commons; use during regular building hours and comply with the library’s quiet-space expectations.

cards.title: Third Floor North Reading Room
cards.subtitle: Guerrieri Academic Commons · third floor
cards.notes: Exit the main elevator on floor three, turn right through the double doors, and set up near the HF–Z general-collection stacks.
cards.short_summary: A named reading room paired with the HF–Z portion of the general collection.
cards.evidence_claim: SU’s wayfinding page identifies the Third Floor North Reading Room and locates the HF–Z general-collection shelves there; third-floor stacks areas are designated quiet spaces.
cards.access_notes: Located in the Guerrieri Academic Commons; use during regular building hours and comply with the library’s quiet-space expectations.

cards.title: Guerrieri Academic Commons Study Carrels
cards.subtitle: Guerrieri Academic Commons · third floor
cards.notes: Reserve an enclosed desk for focused solo work, or check the first-come carrels when a reservation is not needed.
cards.short_summary: Partially enclosed individual desks in quiet third-floor areas.
cards.evidence_claim: The GAC has 28 reservable third-floor study carrels plus first-come carrels; they are enclosed desks located in quiet areas and may be reserved for up to 14 days.
cards.source_title: Reserve a Study Room or Carrel
cards.access_notes: Reservable carrels are on the third floor; additional carrels are first come, first served. Check the online availability schedule before relying on a reserved seat.

cards.entity_name: Guerrieri Academic Commons Group Study Rooms
cards.title: Guerrieri Academic Commons Group Study Rooms
cards.subtitle: Guerrieri Academic Commons · second floor
cards.notes: Book a room sized for four, eight, or ten and bring a device to share work on the room’s TV and whiteboard.
cards.short_summary: Reservable second-floor rooms for small and larger group work.
cards.evidence_claim: SU lists 13 second-floor GAC group study rooms in small, medium, and large sizes for up to 10 people; rooms include a TV and at least one whiteboard.
cards.source_title: Reserve a Study Room or Carrel
cards.access_notes: Study rooms are reservable by SU students, faculty, and staff. Use the room scheduler; unreserved rooms are first come, first served.

cards.entity_name: Guerrieri Academic Commons First-Floor Study Rooms
cards.title: Guerrieri Academic Commons First-Floor Study Rooms
cards.subtitle: Guerrieri Academic Commons · first floor
cards.notes: Check first-floor rooms directly for availability when you need a group workspace without arranging a second-floor reservation.
cards.short_summary: First-floor group rooms available on a first-come basis.
cards.evidence_claim: SU Libraries states that first-floor GAC study rooms are available first come, first served, while second-floor rooms can be reserved online.
cards.access_notes: First-floor rooms are first come, first served. Study rooms have no computers, so bring a device or check out a laptop from the Library Service Desk.

cards.title: GAC Classroom 117
cards.subtitle: Guerrieri Academic Commons · first floor
cards.notes: Look at the availability tablet before settling in; when no library workshop is scheduled, use this technology-enabled classroom as study space.
cards.short_summary: A library classroom that becomes student study space between scheduled uses.
cards.evidence_claim: SU identifies AC 117 as a technology-enabled library classroom and states that classrooms AC 117, 162, and 163 are open as student study spaces when not in use.
cards.access_notes: Available only when not in use during regular GAC hours; current availability is displayed on the tablet outside the room.

cards.title: GAC Classroom 162
cards.subtitle: Guerrieri Academic Commons · first floor
cards.notes: Use the tablet outside the door to confirm the room is open, then take advantage of the classroom setting for a longer work block.
cards.short_summary: A technology-enabled GAC classroom with conditional study access.
cards.evidence_claim: SU identifies AC 162 as a technology-enabled library classroom and states that classrooms AC 117, 162, and 163 are open as student study spaces when not in use.
cards.access_notes: Available only when not in use during regular GAC hours; current availability is displayed on the tablet outside the room.

cards.title: GAC Classroom 163
cards.subtitle: Guerrieri Academic Commons · first floor
cards.notes: Confirm the posted schedule before entering and use the open classroom for study when no workshop, event, or course reservation is active.
cards.short_summary: A technology-enabled classroom that can serve as study space when vacant.
cards.evidence_claim: SU identifies AC 163 as a technology-enabled library classroom and states that classrooms AC 117, 162, and 163 are open as student study spaces when not in use.
cards.access_notes: Available only when not in use during regular GAC hours; current availability is displayed on the tablet outside the room.

cards.title: Jim & Carol Powers Reading Room
cards.subtitle: Dr. Ernie Bond Curriculum Resource Center · Conway Hall
cards.notes: Head to the CRC in Conway Hall and use this named reading room when you want a quiet setting alongside curriculum materials.
cards.short_summary: A quiet reading room within Salisbury’s Curriculum Resource Center.
cards.evidence_claim: SU describes the Jim & Carol Powers Reading Room as one of the CRC spaces where students and faculty can study quietly, individually or in small groups, or relax.
cards.access_notes: The CRC welcomes all SU students, faculty, and staff; it is located in Conway Hall, room TE 226.

cards.entity_name: Guerrieri Academic Commons Cyber-Café Study Space
cards.title: Guerrieri Academic Commons Cyber-Café Study Space
cards.subtitle: Guerrieri Academic Commons · two-story cyber-café
cards.notes: Use the cyber-café’s designated study area for a change of scenery, keeping in mind that dining service and study access can differ.
cards.short_summary: A two-story campus cyber-café with a documented 24-hour study area.
cards.evidence_claim: Salisbury University’s campus facilities page states that the GAC’s two-story cyber-café provides dining as well as 24-hour study space.
cards.access_notes: The university documents 24-hour study space in the two-story cyber-café; confirm building access requirements, as GAC entry can require a Gull Card during certain hours.

boards.title: 10 Blocks Off Campus, One Reason Each
boards.description: Ten named, public-facing stops along corridors in Salisbury’s practical off-campus orbit.

cards.title: Mediterranean Grill
cards.subtitle: South Salisbury Boulevard corridor, across from campus
cards.notes: Use the South Salisbury Boulevard crossing for a meal stop; the restaurant identifies its location as directly across from Salisbury University.
cards.short_summary: A directly opposite-campus restaurant stop.
cards.evidence_claim: Mediterranean Grill states that it is located on South Salisbury Boulevard, right across from Salisbury University.
cards.access_notes: Restaurant service; confirm current hours before going.

cards.title: Salisbury City Park
cards.subtitle: South Park Drive corridor
cards.notes: Enter from the South Park Drive area and choose a trail, picnic table, playground, tennis court, pavilion, or fishing spot for an outdoor break.
cards.short_summary: A large municipal park with varied outdoor amenities.
cards.evidence_claim: The City lists Salisbury City Park along Beaverdam Creek with trails, playground equipment, tennis courts, picnic tables, pavilion, restrooms, bandstand, and fishing.
cards.access_notes: City park facilities are listed as open dawn to dusk; some restrooms operate only during programming or reservations.

cards.title: Salisbury Zoo
cards.subtitle: South Park Drive corridor, within Salisbury City Park
cards.notes: Pair a City Park walk with the zoo grounds and check the zoo’s current visitor details before leaving campus.
cards.short_summary: A zoo set within the City Park landscape.
cards.evidence_claim: Downtown Salisbury identifies Salisbury Zoo as a 12-acre attraction within Salisbury City Park and describes animal exhibits including river otters, wallabies, and flamingos.
cards.access_notes: Confirm current zoo access and visitor information before visiting.

cards.title: City Park Tennis Courts
cards.subtitle: North Park Drive corridor, between Beaver Dam Drive and Main Street
cards.notes: Bring appropriate gear and use the courts off North Park Drive; check the City’s updates for any weather or maintenance interruptions.
cards.short_summary: Public courts on the north edge of City Park.
cards.evidence_claim: The City states that the City Park Tennis Courts are off North Park Drive between Beaver Dam Drive and Main Street and announced their resurfacing completion.
cards.source_title: Game, Set, Match! City Park Tennis Courts Are Back
cards.access_notes: Outdoor courts; check City announcements and weather before use.

cards.title: Salisbury Skate Park
cards.subtitle: South Park Drive corridor, at the edge of City Park
cards.notes: Use the South Park Drive approach for the named skate park, and bring the safety equipment appropriate for your activity.
cards.short_summary: A designated skate facility beside City Park.
cards.evidence_claim: The City’s welcome guide lists Salisbury Skate Park at 926 South Park Drive, and its capital plan places the facility on the edge of City Park.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor facility; observe posted rules and check conditions before use.

cards.title: Unity Square
cards.subtitle: Main Street and Division Street corridor
cards.notes: Meet at the downtown square for its reading garden, public art, splash feature, play areas, and flexible lawn seating.
cards.short_summary: A downtown civic square designed for gathering and play.
cards.evidence_claim: Downtown Salisbury places Unity Square at Division and Main Streets and lists its splash fountain, reading garden, public art, play areas, and seasonal events.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor public space; event programming and splash-feature availability vary seasonally.

cards.title: Salisbury Riverwalk
cards.subtitle: Riverwalk corridor, from Route 13 to the marina
cards.notes: Walk the Wicomico River promenade from the Route 13 end toward the marina, using its seating and boardwalk sections as you go.
cards.short_summary: A riverside pedestrian route through downtown.
cards.evidence_claim: Downtown Salisbury describes the Riverwalk as a concrete promenade along the Wicomico River from Route 13 to the marina, with boardwalk segments and seating.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor pedestrian corridor; use normal waterfront awareness and check event conditions.

cards.title: Riverwalk Games Park
cards.subtitle: Riverwalk corridor
cards.notes: Stop along the Riverwalk for oversized chess, checkers, cornhole, and other outdoor game facilities before continuing downtown.
cards.short_summary: A pocket park focused on casual outdoor games.
cards.evidence_claim: Downtown Salisbury says Riverwalk Games Park has oversized chess and checkers tables, cornhole boards, fire pits, and interactive casual-play facilities.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor recreation area; amenity availability may vary with weather and programming.

cards.title: Pohanka Riverwalk Amphitheater
cards.subtitle: Eastern Riverwalk corridor
cards.notes: Check the event calendar, then use the Riverwalk’s eastern end to find the named outdoor performance venue by the river.
cards.short_summary: An open-air performance venue at the Riverwalk’s east end.
cards.evidence_claim: Downtown Salisbury identifies the Pohanka Riverwalk Amphitheater at the eastern end of the Riverwalk as a venue for performances, Friday Night Live, Movies on the River, and festivals.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor venue; attendance requirements depend on the specific event.

cards.title: Museum of Eastern Shore Culture
cards.subtitle: West Main Street corridor, 218 W. Main Street
cards.notes: Use West Main Street to visit the museum’s Eastern Shore heritage displays, then confirm current exhibition and visitor details before arrival.
cards.short_summary: A downtown museum presenting regional heritage and art.
cards.evidence_claim: Downtown Salisbury lists the Museum of Eastern Shore Culture at 218 W. Main Street and describes exhibits featuring Ward Brothers decoys, SU and local artists, and Native American artifacts.
cards.access_notes: The Downtown Salisbury listing gives Tuesday–Saturday hours; verify current hours and admission information before visiting.

boards.title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
boards.description: Ten documented Salisbury traditions, including active annual events and clearly labeled historical practices.

cards.title: Sing the original school song
cards.subtitle: Salisbury University’s first school song
cards.notes: Look up the original lyrics and connect the song to Salisbury’s 1925 opening-year traditions.
cards.short_summary: The first school song was composed by music faculty member Margaret H. Black in the institution’s first year.
cards.evidence_claim: SU’s centennial history says “Salisbury Normal Here’s to Thee” was composed by Margaret H. Black during the school’s first year of operation.
cards.access_notes: Historical school-song tradition; consult the source for context.

cards.title: Spot Sammy at a Sea Gull event
cards.subtitle: Salisbury University mascot tradition
cards.notes: Bring a camera to a home game or Homecoming and look for Sammy’s photo-op and cheer presence.
cards.short_summary: Sammy is a visible part of athletics, Homecoming, open houses, and campus events.
cards.evidence_claim: SU says Sammy attends Homecoming and Sea Gull Century and appears at home games, open houses, and around campus.
cards.source_title: Sammy Sea Gull: Leader of Sea Gull Nation
cards.access_notes: See SU athletics and event calendars for appearances.

cards.title: Meet Diana’s mischievous campus history
cards.subtitle: Historic graduating-class gift
cards.notes: Read the archival account of the Class of 1931 statue and its many historical relocations and decorations.
cards.short_summary: Diana was a seven-foot plaster statue given to the institution by the Class of 1931.
cards.evidence_claim: SU documents a graduating-class donation tradition and identifies Diana the Huntress as a 1931 class gift.
cards.access_notes: Historical tradition; do not move, alter, or decorate campus artwork.

cards.title: Remember Hands Across Campus
cards.subtitle: Historical campus unity practice
cards.notes: Use the centennial account to learn how participants once formed a hand-holding ring around campus.
cards.short_summary: Beginning in spring 1995, participants joined hands around the center of campus to express cultural harmony.
cards.evidence_claim: SU’s history says Hands Across Campus began in spring 1995 and continued for several years, bringing participants into a ring around campus.
cards.access_notes: Historical practice; the source describes it as occurring from 1995 for several years.

cards.title: Recall the potted-plant welcome
cards.subtitle: Historical new-student tradition
cards.notes: Read the centennial story for this unusual early welcome and compare it with today’s orientation experience.
cards.short_summary: New students once received potted plants during Salisbury’s “Survival of Arrival.”
cards.evidence_claim: SU’s centennial history identifies gifting potted plants to new students during “Survival of Arrival” as a past tradition.
cards.access_notes: Historical practice; this source does not represent it as a current orientation activity.

cards.title: Watch the May the Fourth lightsaber appearance
cards.subtitle: Commons dining-hall tradition
cards.notes: If it is May 4, observe respectfully in the Commons rather than interrupting the staged lightsaber battle.
cards.short_summary: The Knights of Bury have made a surprise May 4 lightsaber appearance in the Commons since 2022.
cards.evidence_claim: SU says the Knights of Bury battle in the Commons every May 4 and that the tradition has run since 2022.
cards.access_notes: Observe only during a scheduled or organized appearance; follow dining-hall staff directions.

cards.title: Follow the Sea Gull Century
cards.subtitle: Annual SU bike-tour tradition
cards.notes: Check the ride’s official information before planning; this tradition began as a student, faculty, and staff century ride.
cards.short_summary: The University Bike Club turned the 1989 first ride into the annual Sea Gull Century.
cards.evidence_claim: SU documents the first Sea Gull Century in 1989 and says the University Bike Club later made it an annual event.
cards.access_notes: Cycling event; verify current registration, route, and safety requirements with organizers.

cards.title: Join The Big Event service day
cards.subtitle: Annual neighborhood thank-you project
cards.notes: Register through current Student Government Association channels and select an assigned outdoor service project.
cards.short_summary: Students volunteer on one day each year to thank Salisbury’s surrounding neighborhoods.
cards.evidence_claim: SU says its SGA adopted The Big Event as an annual project in which students perform outdoor chores for university neighbors.
cards.access_notes: Participate through the organized event and use any required safety guidance or equipment.

cards.title: Look for the University Mace
cards.subtitle: Official academic-ceremony symbol
cards.notes: At a formal academic ceremony, watch for the mace and read its historic-material details before the procession.
cards.short_summary: A 1997 ceremonial mace incorporates wood from a historic Holloway Hall linden tree.
cards.evidence_claim: SU says its mace was first used at the 1997 inauguration and is used at official academic ceremonies, including commencement.
cards.access_notes: View during official ceremonies; do not handle ceremonial objects.

cards.title: Learn about Rat Week beanies
cards.subtitle: Historical new-student custom
cards.notes: Explore the centennial account of this former first-year custom, including its required beanie beginning in 1948.
cards.short_summary: Rat Week began in 1936; its required beanie component continued into the 1970s.
cards.evidence_claim: SU’s centennial history says Rat Week started in 1936, added a required beanie in 1948, and lasted through the 1970s.
cards.source_title: Salisbury. Forever. – A Legacy in Motion
cards.access_notes: Historical tradition, not a current student requirement.

boards.title: Your First Weekend at Salisbury University, Shared as Cards
boards.description: An under-21-safe, campus-centered first-weekend loop using documented spaces for getting oriented, seeing art, moving around campus, and planning the week ahead.

cards.title: Start with the campus map
cards.subtitle: Main campus, Salisbury
cards.notes: Open the official map before setting out, then use its building labels to connect West College, Camden and Dogwood stops.
cards.short_summary: Use the official map to orient your first walk.
cards.evidence_claim: SU identifies West College and Camden Avenues and Dogwood Drive as borders of its main campus and provides a downloadable campus map.
cards.access_notes: Use the online map or download the linked PDF; follow posted parking and access rules.

cards.title: Take an arboretum orientation lap
cards.subtitle: Across Salisbury University’s 200-acre campus
cards.notes: Use the interactive tree map for a self-guided walk and pause at plant labels as you learn the routes between campus buildings.
cards.short_summary: A map-supported walk through SU’s living plant collection.
cards.evidence_claim: The arboretum’s living collections are distributed throughout SU’s 200-acre campus, and the university provides an interactive online tree map.
cards.source_title: The Glenda Chatham Clarke Arboretum | Salisbury University
cards.access_notes: Explore outdoors and use the university’s interactive tree map for route planning.

cards.title: Find Holloway Hall’s linden trees
cards.subtitle: Holloway Hall, main campus
cards.notes: Add this historic tree landmark to your walk, then continue through the nearby academic core without needing an indoor destination.
cards.short_summary: A documented arboretum landmark beside Holloway Hall.
cards.evidence_claim: SU’s arboretum history notes that the institution planted Holloway Hall’s notable linden trees during its first Arbor Day in the 1920s.
cards.source_title: The Glenda Chatham Clarke Arboretum | Salisbury University
cards.access_notes: This is an exterior landmark; respect any building-access rules if entering Holloway Hall.

cards.title: Check the University Gallery schedule
cards.subtitle: Fulton Hall, Room 109
cards.notes: Look at the current exhibition listing before heading over, and plan this indoor art stop only when the gallery schedule confirms it is open.
cards.short_summary: A rotating-exhibition stop in Fulton Hall.
cards.evidence_claim: SU Art Galleries lists the University Gallery in Fulton Hall Room 109 and says its spaces host rotating contemporary art exhibits.
cards.access_notes: Gallery spaces close between exhibits and during university closures; check the gallery schedule first.

cards.title: See what’s on at the Electronic Gallery
cards.subtitle: Conway Hall, Room 128
cards.notes: Pair this with the University Gallery only if both schedules align; it is a separate named gallery space with rotating contemporary work.
cards.short_summary: A second campus gallery in Conway Hall.
cards.evidence_claim: SU Art Galleries identifies the Electronic Gallery in Conway Hall Room 128 as one of its rotating contemporary-art exhibition spaces.
cards.access_notes: Gallery spaces close between exhibits and during university closures; verify the current schedule.

cards.title: Browse Delmarva history at Niemann Gallery
cards.subtitle: Guerrieri Academic Commons, Niemann Gallery
cards.notes: Make this a quiet afternoon stop: enter via the Route 13 side if visiting campus, then take the self-guided exhibit at your pace.
cards.short_summary: A free self-guided exhibit on Delmarva history.
cards.evidence_claim: The Nabb Center describes “Delmarva: People, Place & Time” as an ongoing self-guided Niemann Gallery exhibit and states that events and exhibits are free and open to the public unless otherwise stated.
cards.source_title: Nabb Center Events & Exhibits | Salisbury University
cards.access_notes: Open during Guerrieri Academic Commons hours; campus visitors should use the Route 13-side entrance and arrange the free parking pass if parking.

cards.title: Use the Student Union as your meetup point
cards.subtitle: Guerrieri Student Union, main campus
cards.notes: Choose the central thoroughfare for a low-pressure regroup, then use the building as a landmark before splitting off to later stops.
cards.short_summary: A central campus landmark with a documented 24/7 thoroughfare.
cards.evidence_claim: SU lists the main thoroughfare through the Guerrieri Student Union as open 24/7 and the Fireside Lounge as open daily from 6 a.m. to midnight.
cards.source_title: Building Hours and Codes | Salisbury University
cards.access_notes: The main thoroughfare is listed as 24/7; individual rooms and services can have different access rules.

cards.title: Make a recreation plan at Maggs
cards.subtitle: Maggs Physical Activities Center
cards.notes: Check current facility hours, bring the required Gull Card or membership card, and choose a low-key activity that fits the day’s schedule.
cards.short_summary: SU’s recreation hub for courts, climbing, aquatics, and more.
cards.evidence_claim: SU identifies Maggs Physical Activities Center as a campus recreation facility and says users should bring a Gull Card or membership card for access.
cards.access_notes: Facility access and hours vary; check the current recreation schedule and bring a Gull Card or membership card.

cards.title: Walk by the Outdoor Tennis Center
cards.subtitle: Salisbury University Athletics area
cards.notes: If you have valid card access, plan a casual court session; otherwise use the stop as a clear landmark on an athletics-area walk.
cards.short_summary: Twelve hard-surface tennis courts at SU.
cards.evidence_claim: SU says its Outdoor Tennis Center has 12 hard-surface courts, including six lighted courts, and is home to its varsity tennis teams.
cards.access_notes: Court access is subject to facility policies and current hours; the official facilities page specifies that a Gull Card or membership card is needed for recreation access.

cards.title: Finish with a track-side reset
cards.subtitle: Salisbury University Athletics area
cards.notes: Use the track as the final outdoor landmark, and check current access conditions before planning a walk, run, or spectator stop.
cards.short_summary: An athletics-area stop with a campus-and-community-use track.
cards.evidence_claim: SU states that its resurfaced track is home to men’s and women’s varsity track and field and is open for use by the campus and greater Salisbury community.
cards.access_notes: Check current recreation access conditions and scheduled athletics activity before using the track.
